morning: [happy]Morning{you}! Did you know dew forms because the ground cools faster than the air? I worked that out at dawn!
[laughing]You're up! Good! I need someone to tell me if this leaf smells like lemon or soap.
Oh, morning! Sorry, I've been awake for hours. The night-blooming flowers closed and I wanted to see how.
afternoon: [happy]Hi{you}! Perfect timing. I've got mud on my hands and an idea in my head.
Afternoon! Have you noticed the bees are all going one direction today? Where do you think they're going?
[happy]Hello hello! I just pressed my fortieth kind of flower. Forty! Out of how many, though?
evening: [happy]Evening{you}! The moths are coming out. Did you know some of them only visit one kind of flower?
Oh, is it evening already? I forgot to eat again. Elias is going to scold me.
[happy]Hi! I love dusk. The garden smells completely different. Like it's breathing out.
night: [surprised]You're up late too? I'm watching the glow-moss. It only glows after midnight! Isn't that strange?
It's so late{you}! Can't sleep? Try chamomile. Or counting seeds. I do both.
Shh, listen. That's an owl. I've been trying to find its nest for a week.

rain: [happy]Rain! Everything smells green. Do you think rain has a smell, or is it the earth?
I put out three bowls to measure the rain. Science! Also I wanted to see which bowl the frogs liked.
[laughing]My notes are getting soggy. Worth it. The mushrooms will come up tomorrow.
clear: [happy]Sunny! The flowers are all turned the same way. They follow the sun. Like a little crowd.
Dry day. I need to water the seedlings. Want to help? You can name one.
[happy]Such a bright day. Perfect for drying herbs. The whole house will smell like mint.
storm: [surprised]Lightning! Did you know it's hotter than the sun? Well, I read that. I'd like to test it. Safely.
[worried]The wind's going to flatten my foxgloves. I've staked them, but staking isn't science, it's hope.

work: I'm grinding willow bark. It's for Tomas's knees. Don't tell him, he thinks it's tea.
[happy]Mixing a salve! Beeswax, calendula and a secret ingredient. Okay, the secret's more calendula.
gather: Picking water mint. Careful where you step, there's a frog here I've named Professor.
[happy]Collecting seeds. Each one's a tiny packed lunch for a baby plant. Isn't that lovely?
rest: [happy]I'm resting. Well, I'm reading. Reading's resting for brains. Mostly.
Just sitting. I'm watching an ant carry a crumb ten times its size. I'm cheering for it.
socialize: [happy]Chatting! I asked everyone what their favourite plant is. Mara said 'firewood'.
Lunch at the fire. Sera's telling a story and I'm fact-checking it in my head.
trade: [happy]Buying jars. You can never have too many jars. I have too many jars.
Trading remedies for honey. Fair trade: I fix their coughs, the bees fix my mood.
explore: Exploring! There's a plant near the old ruins I've never seen in any book.
[happy]Just wandering. I find more when I'm not looking. Isn't that annoying?
sleep: Mmh... five more minutes... was I dreaming about roots again?

tired: [sad]I'm so tired. I stayed up reading about mosses. Then I read about the people who read about mosses.
My eyes keep closing mid-sentence. Sorry. What were we... oh, right. You.
[worried]I think I forgot to sleep. Is that possible? I think I did it.
worried: [worried]One of my remedies didn't work and I don't know why. Did I measure wrong? Was it the moon? Was it me?
[worried]I keep worrying I'll make someone sick by mistake. I check everything three times. Then once more.
Sorry, my head's buzzing. There's something wrong with the pond and I can't figure out what.
happy: [laughing]I figured it out! The mint wilts because of the shade from the new fence! Mystery solved!
[happy]I'm so happy today. A seed I planted in spring finally sprouted. I'd given up on it!
[happy]Everything's interesting today. Even the dirt. Especially the dirt.
busy: I'm in the middle of three experiments and one of them is bubbling. Talk fast?
So busy! Hold this jar? Don't shake it. Please don't shake it.

stranger: [happy]You're new! Where are you from? What plants grow there? Do you have strange mushrooms?
Hi! Sorry, I ask a lot of questions. I'll try to ask fewer. I won't manage, but I'll try.
friend: [happy]I like talking to you. You never sigh when I explain things.
You're one of my favourite people to show new plants to. You actually look.
close: [happy]You're my best friend here. Is that okay to say? I'm saying it.
I named a flower after you. It's a weed, technically. But it's a very determined weed.
[happy]I tell you things I don't tell anyone. Like that I'm scared I'm not clever enough. There, I said it again.
wary: [worried]I don't really understand why you were unkind. I want to understand. Can you explain?
I'm being careful around you. I hope I don't have to be forever.

childhood: I grew up in the city beyond the hills. Stone streets, no gardens. I grew beans in a teacup on the windowsill.
[happy]When I was six I tried to dig to the other side of the world. I got as far as a worm. I named him Bertram.
My parents are scholars. Our house was all books and no dirt. I used to sneak out to the park just to touch the grass.
[laughing]I once fed my mother's houseplant ink to see if the flowers would turn blue. They died. Very blue, though.
family: My mother studies old languages and my father studies stars. They wanted me to study something proper. I study weeds.
[sad]They write every month asking when I'll come back to the city. I don't know how to tell them this is home now.
I have a little brother, Pim. He's twelve and wants to be a sailor. I send him dried seahorses I trade from Sera.
My grandmother was a herbalist. She's the only one who understood. I have her old notebook. It's my favourite thing.
background: I came here because my grandmother's notes mentioned a herb that only grows in this valley. I found it in my first week!
I was supposed to stay a month for research. That was three years ago. Oops.
The others thought I was a bit odd at first. Then I cured Elias's cough and suddenly I was 'our Nia'.
work: Every plant is a little medicine cabinet. You just have to learn which drawer is which. And which drawers bite.
Feverfew for headaches, willow for aches, mint for stomachs, and chamomile for when everything's too much.
[happy]I keep a notebook of every remedy and whether it worked. Some pages just say 'no' in big letters.
Medicine is half knowing things and half knowing what you don't know. I'm very good at the second half.
I test everything on myself first. That's why I was purple for a day last spring. Don't ask.
skills: I can name every plant in the village by leaf alone. Well, almost every plant. There's one I'm still arguing with.
[happy]I can make a salve that stops itching in seconds. It smells terrible. But seconds!
I'm good at noticing things. Like that you've got a burr on your sleeve. There. Got it.
hobbies: [happy]I press flowers. I have a book of them, one for every day I've lived here. Some days I cheat and use leaves.
I draw maps of where things grow. My map of the pond has more detail than Mara's map of the village.
I collect interesting stones. Not pretty ones. Interesting ones. There's a difference. I can explain the difference.
ambitions: [happy]I want to write a proper book of every plant in this valley. With drawings! A real book!
One day I'd like to cure something nobody else could. Even something small. Even hiccups.
I'd love a glass house for growing things that hate the cold. Mara says glass is expensive. I say science is priceless.
home: My house smells like twenty different herbs. Visitors either love it or sneeze.
[laughing]There are bunches of herbs hanging from every beam. Tall people have to duck. Mara ducks a lot.
My windowsills are full of seedlings. I've run out of windowsills. I'm eyeing the roof.
furniture: My favourite furniture is my drying rack. Is that furniture? I'm counting it.
[happy]I have a bookshelf that's mostly jars. And a jar shelf that's mostly books. It works for me.
Tomas made me a little stool so I can reach the top shelves. He carved a mushroom on it. I nearly cried.
village: [happy]This village has forty-three kinds of plant within a short walk. I counted. Then I found forty-four.
Everyone here has a skill. Mara builds, Elias grows, Tomas makes, Sera talks. I mix. We're a whole recipe.
I love that people here bring me strange plants to identify. Mostly they're weeds. I love them anyway.
friendship: I think friendship is like a garden. You have to keep showing up, even when nothing seems to be growing.
[happy]Good friends are like good soil. You don't notice them until you see how well everything grows.
I'm not always good at friends. I get distracted. But I always come back.
disagreements: Mara and I argued about whether moss counts as a plant. It does! She said it 'looks like a rug'. That's not a reason!
[worried]Tomas doesn't trust my remedies. He trusts 'the old ways'. My remedies are the old ways, just written down properly!
Sera and I had a fight once about whether her 'dragon scale' was a dragon scale. It was a fish scale. A big fish. Still a fish.
animals: [happy]There's a frog in the pond I've named Professor. He sits on the same lily pad every day. Very dedicated.
Did you know bees dance to tell each other where the flowers are? I tried dancing to tell Elias where the mushrooms were. He didn't get it.
I'd love a cat, but it'd knock over all my jars. Professor the frog is a safer friend.
nature: [happy]Have you ever looked at a leaf really closely? Like, really closely? There are little rivers in it.
The forest is full of mushrooms. Some will heal you, some will kill you, and some will make you see colours. I only pick the first kind.
Everything's connected. The bees need the flowers, the flowers need the rain, the rain needs the sea. It makes my head spin.
seasons: [happy]Spring is the best! Everything's new and I don't know what half of it is yet!
Autumn's when I harvest seeds. It feels like collecting promises.
Winter's when I read and plan. And sneeze. Mostly sneeze.
mornings: I check the dew every morning. Different plants hold it differently. I'm writing a whole chapter on it.
[happy]Mornings smell like possibility. And wet grass. Mostly wet grass.
evenings: [happy]In the evening I write down everything I learned that day. Some days it's a lot. Some days it's 'frogs exist'.
Evenings are for brewing tea and reading by the fire. The perfect experiment.
events: [happy]Festivals are fun! I make everyone a little sprig of something to wear. It's mint, mostly. Mint grows like gossip.
[worried]When the monsters came, I set up a healing corner in the storehouse. I was so scared my hands shook. But I did it.
When a baby's born, I make a little sachet of lavender for the cradle. For calm sleep. And to cover other smells.
worries: [worried]What if I'm not as clever as everyone thinks? What if one day I get it really wrong?
[worried]I worry about my parents. They're getting older and I'm so far away.
I worry that I'll never finish my book. There are too many plants and not enough me.
hopes: [happy]I hope someday a child reads my plant book and decides to become a herbalist too.
I hope my parents come and visit. I'd show them the garden. Maybe they'd understand.
I'd love to find a plant nobody's ever written down. I'd name it after Grandmother.
surprises: [surprised]I found a four-leaf clover today! Then another! Then a five-leaf one! I think the field's mutating. Isn't that exciting?
[surprised]Tomas asked me for a remedy. Tomas! Voluntarily! I nearly dropped my mortar.
funny: [laughing]I once mixed up sugar and dried mustard in Elias's tea. He drank the whole thing to be polite. His eyes watered for an hour.
[laughing]I chased a butterfly halfway to the windmill before I realised I'd left my shoes by the pond.
[laughing]Sera told the travelling tinker I was a witch. He bought six remedies and left very fast. I should thank her, really.

mara: [happy]Mara's brilliant. She can look at a hill and see a house. I look at a hill and see forty plants.
Mara pretends she doesn't need anyone. But she always comes to me when she cuts herself. Which is weekly.
I think Mara's the bravest person here. She just goes and does the scary things. I'd make a list first.
elias: [happy]Elias is the kindest person alive. Scientifically. I've done no studies, but I'm sure.
Elias taught me about soil. He says 'listen to it'. I tried. It didn't say anything. But I knew what he meant.
He always saves me the end of the loaf. He knows it's my favourite. I never told him. He just noticed.
tomas: Tomas is grumpy, but he's grumpy like a hedgehog. Spiky outside, soft inside.
[happy]Tomas tells the best stories about the old days. I write them down when he's not looking.
He calls my remedies 'potions'. I call his furniture 'sticks'. It's our thing.
sera: [laughing]Sera's stories make no sense and I love every one of them. She once told me the moon is a big cheese. I almost checked.
Sera brought me seeds from the coast. She pretends it was a bargain. I know she paid too much.
She's my favourite person to go exploring with. She talks the whole way, but she notices things I miss.

achievement: [happy]You {thing}?! That's amazing! How did you do it? Tell me everything. Step by step.
I heard you {thing}! I'm writing that down. You're going in my notebook.
gift: [happy]For me? Oh! I'm going to keep this forever. Or study it. Possibly both.
[surprised]A gift! Nobody brings me gifts. Except weeds. I love weeds too, but this is better.
house: [happy]Your house is lovely! Can I plant some herbs by your door? Mint keeps the flies away. And it smells nice.
I saw your house! You should put a window box on it. I'll give you seeds.
discovery: [happy]You found {thing}?! Were there any strange plants? Any at all? Please say yes.
You went exploring without me? Next time take me! I'll bring jars.

new_home: [happy]My new house has so many windowsills! I've already filled them all. I need a bigger house.
Moving all my jars took four days. Only two broke. That's a scientific triumph.
partner: [happy]They listen to me talk about moss. For hours! I think that's love. It must be.
I have someone to show all my discoveries to now. Every single one. They're very patient.
child: [happy]My little one already knows what mint smells like! They pull faces at feverfew, though. Fair.
I'm teaching my child to name the flowers. They call everything 'pretty'. Which is accurate.
friend: [happy]When I came here I didn't know anyone. Now people bring me their coughs AND their gossip. That's belonging.
I used to eat lunch alone with a book. Now I eat with friends. The book's a bit jealous.
grief: [sad]I keep thinking if I'd known one more remedy, maybe... Elias says I can't think like that. I try not to.
[sad]I pressed a flower from their garden. It's in my book now. It's the page I open the most.

stories: Do you want to hear how I found the valley herb? It's a good story. I promise it has excitement.
Grandmother's notebook said it grows 'where the water sings and the stones sleep'. Very helpful, Grandmother.
I searched every stream for a week. On the last day I slipped, fell in the river, and landed right next to it.
[laughing]So technically I found it with my face. Science is a lot of falling in rivers, it turns out.
This is a story about Tomas. A nice one. Don't tell him I told you.
Last winter he had a terrible fever. He wouldn't let anyone help. Too proud.
I sat outside his door all night with willow tea, and every hour I just said 'it's here when you want it'.
[happy]At dawn the door opened a crack and a hand came out for the cup. We've never mentioned it since.
I was testing a dye from elderberries and I wanted to see if it stained skin. It did. All of it.
I was purple for a day. Mara called me 'plum'. Sera tried to sell tickets to see me.
[happy]But now I know: elderberry stains skin. Science! I wrote it down in very big letters.
Can I tell you something a bit sad?
Before I came here, I never really fitted anywhere. In the city I was too strange. At school I was too quiet.
The first night here, Elias put a bowl of soup in front of me and said 'eat, we're glad you came'. Just like that.
[happy]I think that's the moment this became home. One bowl of soup. Isn't it funny what matters?

questions.ask: Ooh, question! What's your favourite plant? Or flower? Or tree? Any green thing!

react.rose: [happy]Roses! Beautiful AND you can make tea from the hips. Very practical romance.
react.sunflower: [happy]Sunflowers follow the sun all day! Did you know that? I bet you did. That's why you picked it.
react.oak: [happy]Oaks! They can live a thousand years. Imagine what they've seen.
react.lavender: [happy]Lavender! For calm and sleep. You have a peaceful heart, I think.
react.mint: [laughing]Mint! It grows everywhere and you can never get rid of it. Like me!
react.daisy: [happy]Daisies close at night! Like they're going to sleep. That's my favourite fact.
react.other: [happy]{answer}! I'll look that up. Or find one. Or both!

questions.recall: You said your favourite was {answer}. I've been looking for some to press for you.

questions.ask: Have you ever wondered why the sky is blue? I have a theory. Do you want to hear it?

react.yes: [happy]The air is full of tiny bits that scatter blue light more than red! I think. I'm mostly sure. Isn't that wonderful?
react.no: [laughing]That's fair. Nobody ever wants to hear it. I'll tell the frogs.
react.other: I'll take that as a maybe. I'll save the theory for later!

questions.recall: Remember when I told you about the sky? I've got a new theory about sunsets now.

questions.ask: Do you like reading? I could lend you a book. I have so many. Too many.

react.yes: [happy]I'll lend you my grandmother's favourite. Be careful, it's held together with thread and hope.
react.no: That's alright! I'll just tell you what's in them instead. That's probably worse, isn't it.
react.other: Well, my door's open if you ever want one.

recall.yes: You told me you love reading. I've picked out a book for you!
recall.no: You said you don't read much. I found a book with pictures. Lots of pictures. No pressure!
recall.other: I've picked out a book for you, just in case.

questions.ask: Where's the most interesting place you've been in the valley? I want to go everywhere.

react.lake: [happy]The forest lake! I bet there are water plants there I've never seen.
react.ruins: [surprised]The old ruins? There's a plant growing in the stones there I can't name. It's driving me mad.
react.windmill: [happy]The windmill! The grass around it is full of clover. The bees love it.
react.forest: The woods? Be careful. But tell me what mushrooms you saw. Please.
react.pond: [laughing]The pond! That's where Professor lives. Did you say hello?
react.watchtower: The watchtower! You can see the whole valley from up there. I want to map it.
react.other: {answer}? I've never been! I'm going to go. You have to show me.

questions.recall: You said {answer} was the most interesting place. I went! You were right!
